evidence.source: Shuowen.org, Shuowen Jiezi and Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.text: The entry records 說，釋也，从言、兌, and a second gloss 一曰談說. Duan Yucai reads the first gloss as explaining/releasing and associates it with joy; his note says 兌 is phonetic and also discusses a semantic association. These are historical lexicographic analyses, not independent evidence of the graph’s earliest formation.
evidence.title: 說文解字「說」

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說 entry; notes, senses, example citations and form table
evidence.text: The dictionary gives the traditional analysis 从言、兊 and the later explicit formulation 从言，兌聲. It lists shuō, shuì, and yuè and separates uses including discussion, explanation, reporting, admonishing/persuading, and joy. Its cited examples include the Analects and Book of Songs for joy; these establish uses in those transmitted texts but do not by themselves date the wording or establish a semantic chronology. The table identifies Shuowen forms and later sources; the Han-slip image is marked unpublished.
evidence.title: [A03839] 說 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說 entry; writing-form notes and variant character history
evidence.text: The dictionary notes 説 among the variants of 說. It records a scribal-form explanation for some later variants involving confusion between 口 and ㄙ in clerical writing, but this explanation concerns those variant shapes and is not evidence for the origin of the ancient graph 說.
evidence.title: [A03839] 說 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1, 20 September 2014
evidence.text: The authors describe this downloadable table as almost 5,000 items with separate pinyin, Middle Chinese transcription, and Old Chinese reconstruction columns. The dataset distinguishes Middle Chinese notation from reconstructed Old Chinese notation. Its PDF endpoint failed to open in this inspection; exact character readings are therefore not asserted from the page. The packet’s local Baxter–Sagart rows for 説 give OC *l̥ot-s, *l̥ot, *lot for distinct glosses, but no 兌 row; these local rows are not evidence that sound role was established.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1

evidence.field: 說 character entry and character relations
evidence.text: The search result identifies 説 as an alternate form (U+8AAC) and 说 as the simplified character (U+8BF4), and reports the traditional graph under 言 plus seven strokes. The entry itself could not be opened, so this is discovery-level evidence only and is not relied on for detailed historical claims.
evidence.title: 說 - Chinese Text Project

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The record cites the mainland Simplified Character List, third table, for the variant shape 说-related component classification; it supports a simplified-form relation for the component form when read with that official table, but is not by itself a component paleography source.
evidence.title: [A03839-006] (說) - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Wikimedia Commons, exact file description page
evidence.field: File summary, source, permission, licensing and original file
evidence.text: The page identifies 說-seal.svg as a digitally created depiction of 說 in Shuowen seal-script style and gives source references including Sinica Database, Chinese Etymology, and an image record S01728 on Hanziyuan. It states public-domain release for this SVG representation of an ancient script. This is a modern redraw, not a photograph of an ancient artifact. The page’s Original file link established the direct image URL.

evidence.source: Wikimedia Commons, exact file description page
evidence.text: The inspected Original file link points to https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/67/%E8%AA%AA-seal.svg. The browsing tool rejected rendering the SVG content type, but the direct URL is the link supplied by the verified file description page.
evidence.title: File:說-seal.svg - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.source: 中华人民共和国国务院 / Wikisource transcription of 1986 Simplified Character List
evidence.field: List preface, simplified radical rules, and third table
evidence.text: The 1986 transcription explains that the standardized list uses brackets for traditional forms, classifies 讠 as a simplified radical generally used on the left, and in the third table lists 说〔説〕. This supports 说 as a standardized simplified counterpart of 説, a recognized variant of 說, and supports 讠 as the simplified left-side form of 言 in this graph. The rendered transcription is hosted by Wikisource, which cites the State Language Commission source.
evidence.title: 简化字总表（1986年版）

evidence.text: The official per-codepoint lookup pages for 说 U+8BF4, 說 U+8AAA, and 兌 U+514C could not be opened in the browsing tool. Packet-local Unihan rows give kMandarin shuō for 说 and 說, but no 兌 row is provided. These current readings are metadata, not evidence for an ancient sound relationship.
evidence.title: Unihan Database Lookup

gaps: No primary paleographic image or dated manuscript edition for 說 was verified. The earliest graphic attestation is unresolved; secondary sources show a Warring States/Chu form sequence, but the Taiwan MOE table does not publish its Han-slip image.

No securely dated earliest occurrence of the spoken senses was established. MOE’s citations document multiple uses and quotations in received texts, but the dated history and transmission of those passages need independent textual scholarship.

The 兌 role as phonetic is explicitly given by Shuowen/Duan and the MOE dictionary; independent same-system Baxter–Sagart comparison remains unavailable because the PDF failed and local table has no 兌 row. Traditional *l̥ot, *l̥ot-s, *lot readings for 説 are packet-local rows; do not silently equate them with Zhengzhang *hljod(s)/ *lod variants.

No exact official Unihan click-through record for 说, 說, or 兌 could be opened. Provided local kMandarin rows report shuō for 说 and 說; no component row for 兌 was supplied. Current component pronunciation therefore remains unchecked.

No independent evidence was found that 兌 contributes meaning to the compound. Duan Yucai’s suggestion that it is semantically involved is an historical lexicographic interpretation; the common graph analysis treats 言 as semantic and 兌 as phonetic.

The glyph image is a modern vector reconstruction in Shuowen seal style; no pixel inspection was performed in this stage. It should not be described as an artifact photograph. A likely Chu manuscript candidate was not selected because its actual exact source image and attribution were not established.
No Xiaoxuetang results were returned. No image from that source is proposed.
No tracked extract recommended: sources were used for character-specific paraphrase, and broad reuse rights for their dictionary text were not established.
